# Who will rule the world? Ronaldo leads star-studded race for FIFA’s top honor

As the football world turns its attention to the 2008 FIFA World Player of the Year award, the field is packed with familiar brilliance, rising greatness and the glow of a triumphant European Championship summer.

Cristiano Ronaldo appears to be the frontrunner after a remarkable year with Manchester United, but Lionel Messi, Fernando Torres, Kaká and Xavi all have compelling cases built on club dominance, international impact or both.

Here is a look at the leading candidates and the achievements that define their bids.

## Cristiano Ronaldo — Manchester United and Portugal

If the award is judged primarily on club football, Cristiano Ronaldo’s case is difficult to beat.

The Manchester United winger produced the best season of his career in 2007-08, scoring 42 goals in all competitions and driving Sir Alex Ferguson’s side to a Premier League and UEFA Champions League double. His blend of pace, power, aerial ability and spectacular finishing made him the most decisive player in Europe.

Ronaldo finished as the Premier League’s top scorer and won the European Golden Shoe, an extraordinary achievement for a player who was not a traditional center-forward. In the Champions League final against Chelsea in Moscow, he scored United’s goal in a 1-1 draw before his side eventually won on penalties.

For Portugal, Ronaldo’s Euro 2008 was more mixed. He scored against the Czech Republic and helped his country reach the quarterfinals, but Portugal was eliminated by Germany. Still, his club achievements were so overwhelming that his international shortcomings may not be enough to loosen his grip on the award.

**Case for the award:** Best player on Europe’s best club team, prolific scorer, Champions League winner.  
**Question mark:** Portugal fell short at Euro 2008.

## Lionel Messi — Barcelona and Argentina

Lionel Messi’s 2008 was not quite as decorated at club level as Ronaldo’s, but his individual brilliance continued to suggest that he was football’s next defining genius.

Barcelona endured a disappointing 2007-08 campaign, finishing third in La Liga and failing to win a major trophy. Yet Messi remained the club’s most electrifying player when fit, dazzling opponents with his close control, acceleration and left-footed finishing. His performances helped Barcelona reach the Champions League semifinals, where they were eliminated by Manchester United.

Internationally, Messi strengthened his case by helping Argentina win gold at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. Though the Olympic tournament does not carry the weight of the World Cup or Copa América, Messi was central to Argentina’s attack and played a key role in a talented side that also featured Sergio Agüero, Ángel Di María and Juan Román Riquelme.

Messi may not have the trophy haul of Ronaldo in 2008, but his reputation as one of the world’s most gifted players is beyond dispute.

**Case for the award:** Outstanding individual talent; Olympic gold with Argentina.  
**Question mark:** Barcelona finished the season without a major trophy.

## Fernando Torres — Liverpool and Spain

Fernando Torres made an immediate and spectacular impact in English football after joining Liverpool from Atlético Madrid.

In his first Premier League season, Torres scored 24 league goals and 33 in all competitions, giving Liverpool a world-class cutting edge and quickly becoming one of the most feared strikers in Europe. His pace, movement and calm finishing made him a nightmare for defenders.

But it was on the international stage that Torres produced the year’s defining moment. In the Euro 2008 final against Germany, he scored the only goal of the match, lifting the ball past Jens Lehmann and delivering Spain its first major international trophy in 44 years.

Torres was not Spain’s most consistent player throughout the tournament, but his final-winning goal gave him a historic place in Spanish football. Combined with his superb debut season at Liverpool, it makes him one of the strongest challengers to Ronaldo.

**Case for the award:** Brilliant first season at Liverpool; scored the winning goal in the Euro 2008 final.  
**Question mark:** Liverpool did not win a major trophy.

## Kaká — AC Milan and Brazil

Kaká entered 2008 as the reigning FIFA World Player of the Year and Ballon d’Or winner, but this year has been less commanding than his extraordinary 2007.

At club level, AC Milan struggled domestically, finishing fifth in Serie A and missing out on Champions League qualification for the following season. Kaká still produced moments of elegance and invention, remaining Milan’s creative leader, but injuries and the team’s inconsistency limited his influence.

His best recent achievements — including Milan’s 2007 Champions League triumph and the FIFA Club World Cup victory later that year — still linger in voters’ memories, but the 2008 award is likely to reward more current success.

For Brazil, Kaká remained one of the national team’s marquee names, though his international year was not as defining as those of Spain’s Euro 2008 winners or Messi’s Olympic campaign.

**Case for the award:** Reigning holder; still one of football’s elite playmakers.  
**Question mark:** Milan’s poor season and lack of major 2008 silverware weaken his bid.

## Xavi — Barcelona and Spain

If the award recognizes influence rather than headlines, Xavi has a serious claim.

At Barcelona, Xavi was the metronome of the midfield, controlling tempo with his passing, intelligence and positioning. Although the club did not win a major trophy in 2007-08, his consistency was rarely in doubt.

His international year, however, was exceptional. Xavi was the heartbeat of Spain’s Euro 2008-winning team, setting the rhythm for a side that transformed international football with its possession-based style. His performances earned him UEFA’s Player of the Tournament award.

While Torres scored the final’s decisive goal, Xavi embodied Spain’s identity. His passing and control allowed Spain to dominate matches and finally shed its reputation for underachievement on the international stage.

Midfield organizers rarely win individual awards ahead of prolific scorers, but Xavi’s Euro 2008 influence gives him one of the most intellectually compelling cases.

**Case for the award:** Euro 2008 champion and player of the tournament; central to Spain’s style.  
**Question mark:** Lacks the goal-scoring numbers and club trophies of Ronaldo.

## The verdict: Ronaldo remains the man to beat

The 2008 race features several worthy candidates. Messi dazzled, Torres delivered the most iconic international moment, Kaká retained his aura, and Xavi orchestrated Spain’s golden summer.

But Cristiano Ronaldo’s year stands above the rest.

His goal-scoring numbers, Premier League dominance and Champions League triumph make him the clear favorite. In a year when Manchester United ruled Europe and Ronaldo was its most devastating weapon, the Portuguese star appears poised to claim football’s highest individual honor.

## Ronaldo’s trophy-laden year

Ronaldo enters the vote as the clear favorite after a remarkable campaign with Manchester United. The 23-year-old scored **42 goals in all competitions during the 2007-08 season**, helping Sir Alex Ferguson’s side win both the **Premier League** and the **UEFA Champions League**.

His domestic league form was decisive. Ronaldo finished as the **Premier League’s top scorer with 31 goals**, equaling the record for a 38-game season, and added crucial goals in Europe as United returned to the summit of the continental game.

In May, United defeated Chelsea in the Champions League final in Moscow. Ronaldo scored United’s goal in the 1-1 draw before missing in the penalty shootout, but his side survived to lift the trophy after Edwin van der Sar saved Nicolas Anelka’s attempt.

Ronaldo’s year has already brought him the **Ballon d’Or**, awarded by France Football, and the FIFA honor would complete a sweep of the game’s two leading individual prizes.

With Portugal, Ronaldo was part of the squad that reached the quarterfinals of **Euro 2008**, where they were eliminated by Germany. While his international tournament did not match his club form, his overall impact across the year has made him the leading candidate.

His future has also been a constant subject of speculation, with **Real Madrid** repeatedly linked with a move for the Portuguese star. United insisted during the summer of 2008 that he would remain at Old Trafford, and Ronaldo began the 2008-09 season in Manchester after recovering from ankle surgery.

## Messi emerges as Barcelona’s central figure

If Ronaldo’s case is built on trophies and numbers, Messi’s is based on influence, artistry and the sense that Barcelona’s attack increasingly revolves around him.

The Argentine forward enjoyed another outstanding year at the Camp Nou, despite Barcelona finishing the 2007-08 season without a major trophy. Messi’s pace, close control and left-footed finishing made him one of the most feared players in Europe, and his importance has only increased under new coach Pep Guardiola.

By early 2009, Barcelona were setting the pace in **La Liga**, playing the high-tempo, possession-based football that has quickly defined Guardiola’s first season in charge. Messi, alongside Samuel Eto’o and Thierry Henry, has been central to a team that has scored freely and opened a significant lead over its domestic rivals.

Messi also enjoyed success with **Argentina**, winning the **Olympic gold medal in Beijing** in August 2008. He played a key role in Argentina’s run, supplying decisive moments in a side that also featured Sergio Aguero, Angel Di Maria and Juan Roman Riquelme.

Although the FIFA World Player award has often favored players with major club trophies, Messi’s performances have kept him close to Ronaldo in the voting conversation.

## Torres carries Liverpool and Spain

Fernando Torres’ nomination confirms his status as one of the game’s elite strikers after a stunning first year at Liverpool and a decisive role in Spain’s European Championship triumph.

Torres scored **33 goals in all competitions for Liverpool in 2007-08**, including **24 in the Premier League**, the highest total by a foreign player in a debut Premier League season at the time. His pace, movement and clinical finishing quickly made him the focal point of Rafael Benitez’s attack.

Liverpool did not win a trophy in 2008, but Torres’ individual form helped the club reach the Champions League semifinals and remain competitive near the top of English football.

His defining moment, however, came in a Spain shirt. Torres scored the only goal in the **Euro 2008 final**, lifting the ball past Germany goalkeeper Jens Lehmann to give Spain a 1-0 victory in Vienna.

That goal ended Spain’s 44-year wait for a major international trophy and helped change the country’s footballing identity from perennial underachievers to champions.

## Xavi rewarded for Spain’s midfield mastery

Xavi’s place on the shortlist reflects the growing recognition of midfield control as much as goalscoring brilliance.

The Barcelona midfielder was named **Player of the Tournament at Euro 2008**, where he orchestrated Spain’s passing game alongside Marcos Senna, Andres Iniesta, Cesc Fabregas and David Silva. Spain’s style — patient, technical and precise — became the story of the tournament, and Xavi was its conductor.

For Barcelona, Xavi has remained central during a period of transition. After the end of the Frank Rijkaard era, Guardiola has built his team around pressing, movement and possession, principles that suit Xavi’s game perfectly.

Though he lacks the spectacular scoring statistics of Ronaldo, Messi or Torres, Xavi’s nomination highlights the importance of Spain’s Euro 2008 success and Barcelona’s resurgence.

## Kaka remains among elite despite Milan transition

Kaka, the 2007 FIFA World Player of the Year, returns to the shortlist after another influential year with AC Milan. The Brazilian playmaker did not enjoy the same collective success as in 2007, when Milan won the Champions League, but he remained one of the sport’s most admired attacking midfielders.

Milan missed out on the 2008-09 Champions League after finishing fifth in Serie A the previous season, leaving Kaka outside Europe’s top competition during the second half of the year. Even so, his creativity, dribbling and ability to score from midfield kept him in the global conversation.

Like Ronaldo, Kaka has also been linked with major transfer speculation, including interest from some of Europe’s richest clubs. **Real Madrid**, amid another period of rebuilding and presidential politics, has long admired both Kaka and Ronaldo as potential symbols of a new era at the Bernabeu.

## Spain’s golden year shapes the vote

The 2008 award comes after a year in which Spain enjoyed its greatest international success in decades. Luis Aragones’ side won Euro 2008 with a brand of football that emphasized possession, technical quality and collective intelligence.

That victory helped elevate Torres and Xavi into the FIFA shortlist and strengthened the reputations of Spain’s wider generation, including Iker Casillas, Carles Puyol, Iniesta, David Villa and Sergio Ramos.

At club level, Spanish football also remained central to the global game. Barcelona’s revival under Guardiola has made Messi and Xavi major contenders, while Real Madrid’s pursuit of superstar signings has continued to dominate headlines despite the club’s uneven European record in recent seasons.

## Premier League influence still strong

Manchester United’s Champions League triumph ensured that English football remained at the center of the 2008 conversation. United beat Chelsea in Moscow, while Liverpool again reached the latter stages of Europe’s top competition.

Ronaldo and Torres, the Premier League’s two most devastating attacking players during the year, both finished among the finalists. Their inclusion underlines the league’s growing global pull and its ability to attract and develop world-class talent.

For United, Ronaldo’s nomination is another reminder of the club’s dominance in 2008. For Liverpool, Torres’ recognition reflects his rapid transformation from promising Atletico Madrid captain to one of the most feared forwards in world football.

## The expected outcome

While all five nominees have strong cases, Ronaldo’s combination of goals, trophies and individual honors makes him the overwhelming favorite.

A FIFA World Player victory would cap a year in which he moved from elite winger to global superstar, delivering the numbers of a striker while retaining the flair and unpredictability of a wide player.

Messi appears his closest challenger, with many observers viewing the Argentine as the player most likely to dominate the award in future years. Torres and Xavi carry the weight of Spain’s historic summer, while Kaka remains a symbol of established world-class excellence.

The winner will be announced at FIFA’s gala in Zurich, where football’s leading coaches and captains will decide whether Ronaldo’s golden year with Manchester United is enough to place him officially at the top of the world game.
